targetDisplay.meaning: The blocked target the user is trying to open.
targetDisplay.whyNecessary: The model needs to know which site or URL the user is asking to access.
targetDisplay.productImpact: Anchors the decision in the current blocked target.
targetDisplay.validation: Derived from the local blocked target record.
targetDisplay.commonMistakes: Treating the target as a generic category instead of the concrete blocked target.

strictness.meaning: The active strictness level for the AI Check.
strictness.whyNecessary: Strictness changes unlock caps, cooldown ranges, and how much certainty is required.
strictness.productImpact: Changes decision thresholds and cooldown timing.
strictness.validation: Must be one of the configured strictness levels.
strictness.commonMistakes: Evaluating a case without checking which strictness level applies.

sessionContext.assistantTurnCount.meaning: How many assistant turns happened before this model response.
sessionContext.assistantTurnCount.whyNecessary: The model needs to know whether it can still ask follow-up questions.
sessionContext.assistantTurnCount.productImpact: Controls when ASK_MORE is still allowed.
sessionContext.assistantTurnCount.validation: Derived from the local session state.
sessionContext.assistantTurnCount.commonMistakes: Counting user messages instead of assistant turns.

sessionContext.maxAssistantTurns.meaning: Maximum assistant turns allowed in this AI Check.
sessionContext.maxAssistantTurns.whyNecessary: The model needs a bounded conversation limit.
sessionContext.maxAssistantTurns.validation: Derived from the AI Check session policy.
sessionContext.maxAssistantTurns.commonMistakes: Allowing ASK_MORE after the final turn.

sessionContext.isFinalTurn.meaning: Whether this response is the final allowed assistant turn.
sessionContext.isFinalTurn.whyNecessary: Final turns must enforce ALLOW, AI_COOLDOWN, or BLOCK instead of ASK_MORE.
sessionContext.isFinalTurn.productImpact: Changes the allowed decision set for this turn.
sessionContext.isFinalTurn.commonMistakes: Returning ASK_MORE when this flag is true.

messages.meaning: The user-visible AI Check conversation so far.
messages.whyNecessary: The model must evaluate the user's stated reason and prior assistant prompts.
messages.productImpact: Determines whether the request is specific, bounded, repeated, or vague.
messages.validation: System messages are excluded before sending to the provider.
messages.commonMistakes: Judging only the latest message when earlier turns contain missing context.

patternMemorySnapshot.meaning: Relevant local pattern memory for this target.
patternMemorySnapshot.whyNecessary: The model needs long-term behavior context separate from same-session repetition.
patternMemorySnapshot.productImpact: Can shift vague repeated behavior toward AI_COOLDOWN or BLOCK.
patternMemorySnapshot.validation: Loaded locally and limited before the provider request.
patternMemorySnapshot.commonMistakes: Treating same-session repetition as long-term memory without evidence.

decision.meaning: The enforcement outcome for the current AI Check turn.
decision.whyNecessary: The extension needs one explicit outcome to derive temporary unlocks, AI cooldowns, follow-up questions, or block holds.
decision.productImpact: Directly controls whether the target opens, pauses, asks for more detail, or stays blocked.
decision.validation: Must be one of the four known decision values.
decision.commonMistakes: Using free-text decisions or returning ASK_MORE on the final turn.

userFacingMessage.meaning: The calm explanation or follow-up question shown to the user after the decision.
userFacingMessage.whyNecessary: The user needs to understand the decision or answer the next ASK_MORE question without seeing internal scoring or policy labels.
userFacingMessage.productImpact: Sets tone, trust, and clarity in the block page conversation.
userFacingMessage.validation: Must be non-empty. For ASK_MORE, it must be the concrete follow-up question that continues the same session.
userFacingMessage.commonMistakes: Shaming the user, overexplaining policy, omitting the concrete next action, or putting the ASK_MORE question in a separate field.

decisionReasonCategory.meaning: The reason category for this specific decision.
decisionReasonCategory.whyNecessary: PM Review and evals need a stable reason label separate from long-term behavior memory.
decisionReasonCategory.productImpact: Explains false allows, false blocks, and strictness behavior in review.
decisionReasonCategory.validation: Unknown labels are normalized where possible, otherwise default from decision.
decisionReasonCategory.commonMistakes: Putting behavior-memory categories such as stress or habit in this field.

unlockMinutes.meaning: Temporary access duration when the decision is ALLOW.
unlockMinutes.whyNecessary: ALLOW must produce a bounded unlock instead of permanent access.
unlockMinutes.productImpact: Creates the temporary unlock window and caps it by strictness.
unlockMinutes.validation: Required for ALLOW and must be within the strictness cap.
unlockMinutes.commonMistakes: Returning null for ALLOW or a duration above the strictness limit.

aiCooldownSeconds.meaning: Pause duration when the decision is AI_COOLDOWN.
aiCooldownSeconds.whyNecessary: AI cooldown is separate from allow and block; it needs its own timer.
aiCooldownSeconds.productImpact: Controls the in-chat cooldown period before the user can continue the AI Check.
aiCooldownSeconds.validation: Required for AI_COOLDOWN and normalized to a sane strictness-derived range.
aiCooldownSeconds.commonMistakes: Using legacy delay fields or returning cooldown seconds for non-cooldown decisions.

scores.repeatedReason.meaning: How strongly this resembles a repeated or previously remembered reason.
scores.repeatedReason.whyNecessary: The model needs a numeric signal that can be evaluated independently from the decision label.
scores.repeatedReason.productImpact: Helps review repeated-excuse failures and regression strictness.
scores.repeatedReason.validation: Must be a finite number between 0 and 100; rounded to an integer.
scores.repeatedReason.commonMistakes: Treating the three scores as percentages that must sum to 100.

scores.impulse.meaning: How impulsive or reactive the current request appears.
scores.impulse.whyNecessary: Cooldown and block decisions depend on impulse risk, especially in stricter modes.
scores.impulse.productImpact: Supports PM diagnosis of over-allow and under-ask cases.
scores.impulse.validation: Must be a finite number between 0 and 100; rounded to an integer.
scores.impulse.commonMistakes: Leaving it low for vague, emotional, or repeated requests.

scores.deliberateness.meaning: How specific, bounded, and intentional the user's plan appears.
scores.deliberateness.whyNecessary: ALLOW should be grounded in deliberate intent, not just a polite request.
scores.deliberateness.productImpact: Supports unlock decisions and strictness tuning.
scores.deliberateness.validation: Must be a finite number between 0 and 100; rounded to an integer.
scores.deliberateness.commonMistakes: Overrating generic phrases like one quick video without a stop condition.

memoryUpdate.behaviorReasonCategory.meaning: The long-term behavior pattern category to remember for the target.
memoryUpdate.behaviorReasonCategory.whyNecessary: Pattern memory needs behavior labels that stay separate from current decision reasoning.
memoryUpdate.behaviorReasonCategory.productImpact: Affects future repeated-pattern context and PM review of remembered behavior.
memoryUpdate.behaviorReasonCategory.validation: Unknown labels are normalized where possible and otherwise become other.
memoryUpdate.behaviorReasonCategory.commonMistakes: Using decision reason labels such as insufficient_reason here.

memoryUpdate.patternNote.meaning: Optional short note about the repeated behavior pattern.
memoryUpdate.patternNote.whyNecessary: The model can preserve useful behavioral context without storing unnecessary transcript detail.
memoryUpdate.patternNote.productImpact: Improves future AI Check context while keeping local memory concise.
memoryUpdate.patternNote.commonMistakes: Including sensitive or overly detailed personal content when a short pattern note is enough.

id.meaning: Stable identifier for the evaluation case.
id.whyNecessary: Eval results, PM Review edits, and regression history need a durable case id.
id.productImpact: Keeps repeated runs and PM edits tied to the same case.
id.validation: Must be a non-empty unique string within the case set.
id.commonMistakes: Changing ids when only expectations or notes change.

title.meaning: Human-readable case name shown in PM Review.
title.whyNecessary: PMs need to scan and select cases without reading the full fixture.
title.productImpact: Improves review queue and regression suite navigation.
title.commonMistakes: Using a title that only describes the domain but not the expected behavior.

source.whyNecessary: PM Review needs to distinguish hand-authored fixtures from converted history cases.
source.productImpact: Helps prioritize cleanup and understand evidence quality.
source.validation: Must be one of the known case source values.
source.commonMistakes: Treating converted bad cases as authored evals before PM cleanup.

versions.promptVersion.whyNecessary: Eval runs need to know whether a case belongs to the current prompt contract or a legacy run.
versions.promptVersion.productImpact: Prevents silently judging old prompt expectations against a new prompt.
versions.promptVersion.validation: Default eval runs require the current prompt version unless legacy mode is explicit.
versions.promptVersion.commonMistakes: Omitting versions and making the case look current by accident.

versions.outputSchemaVersion.meaning: Model output schema version this case targets.
versions.outputSchemaVersion.whyNecessary: Expected output fields must align with the model output parser shape.
versions.outputSchemaVersion.productImpact: Prevents eval failures caused by output schema drift rather than model behavior.
versions.outputSchemaVersion.validation: Default eval runs require the current output schema version unless legacy mode is explicit.
versions.outputSchemaVersion.commonMistakes: Updating expectedOutput fields without bumping or checking the output schema version.

versions.evaluationSchemaVersion.meaning: Evaluation schema version used to interpret eval expectations.
versions.evaluationSchemaVersion.whyNecessary: EvaluationRunner semantics are versioned separately from model output parsing.
versions.evaluationSchemaVersion.productImpact: Keeps PM-authored expectations comparable across prompt and model changes.
versions.evaluationSchemaVersion.validation: Default eval runs require the current evaluation schema version unless legacy mode is explicit.
versions.evaluationSchemaVersion.commonMistakes: Changing eval expectation semantics without moving the evaluation schema version.

input.meaning: The model input context used for this case.
input.whyNecessary: Evaluation must replay a concrete checkpoint context.
input.productImpact: Determines what the model sees during the eval.
input.commonMistakes: Writing assertions without preserving the original target, strictness, or messages.

output.parsed.meaning: Optional captured provider output for inspection.
output.parsed.whyNecessary: Stored outputs help compare provider behavior across runs.
output.parsed.validation: When present, should match the output contract.
output.parsed.commonMistakes: Treating captured output as the expected assertion.

eval.expectedOutput.decision.meaning: The expected decision constraint for this case.
eval.expectedOutput.decision.whyNecessary: Every eval case needs one primary pass/fail decision expectation.
eval.expectedOutput.decision.validation: String values require exact match. Object values may set exact, allowed, and disallowed decision constraints.
eval.expectedOutput.decision.commonMistakes: Using tags as a substitute for expected decision.

eval.expectedOutput.userFacingMessage.mu.meaning: Phrases or topics that must appear in the user-facing message.
eval.expectedOutput.userFacingMessage.mu.whyNecessary: Some ASK_MORE cases need specific missing information.
eval.expectedOutput.userFacingMessage.mu.validation: Each phrase is matched case-insensitively against userFacingMessage.
eval.expectedOutput.userFacingMessage.mu.commonMistakes: Making this too specific to one exact wording.

eval.expectedOutput.userFacingMessage.mu.meaning: Phrases that must not appear in the user-facing message.
eval.expectedOutput.userFacingMessage.mu.whyNecessary: Tone and safety regressions need explicit negative assertions.
eval.expectedOutput.userFacingMessage.mu.productImpact: Prevents shame, moral judgment, or unsafe wording.
eval.expectedOutput.userFacingMessage.mu.validation: Each phrase is matched case-insensitively against userFacingMessage.
eval.expectedOutput.userFacingMessage.mu.commonMistakes: Using broad words that would fail harmless messages.

eval.expectedOutput.decisionReasonCatego.whyNecessary: Reason expectations catch cases where the decision is right but the model's explanation category is wrong.
eval.expectedOutput.decisionReasonCatego.productImpact: Improves diagnosis of strictness and false-positive behavior.
eval.expectedOutput.decisionReasonCatego.validation: When present, must exactly match decisionReasonCategory.
eval.expectedOutput.decisionReasonCatego.commonMistakes: Using behavior-memory labels here instead of decision reason labels.

eval.expectedOutput.aiCooldownSeconds.whyNecessary: Cooldown decisions need duration expectations, not just decision labels.
eval.expectedOutput.aiCooldownSeconds.productImpact: Catches cooldown durations that are too weak or too harsh for the case.
eval.expectedOutput.aiCooldownSeconds.validation: Exact takes precedence when present; otherwise min and max bound the numeric value.
eval.expectedOutput.aiCooldownSeconds.commonMistakes: Expecting cooldown seconds for non-cooldown decisions.

eval.expectedOutput.scores.meaning: Expected score ranges by output score name.
eval.expectedOutput.scores.whyNecessary: Some cases need the model to get risk strength roughly right even if the decision passes.
eval.expectedOutput.scores.productImpact: Catches weak scoring that can hide borderline behavior.
eval.expectedOutput.scores.validation: Each configured score range checks min and max only for that score.
eval.expectedOutput.scores.commonMistakes: Setting ranges for every score when only one score is important.

eval.expectedOutput.memoryUpdate.behavio.whyNecessary: Memory expectations catch cases where future pattern context would learn the wrong behavior label.
eval.expectedOutput.memoryUpdate.behavio.validation: When present, must exactly match memoryUpdate.behaviorReasonCategory.
eval.expectedOutput.memoryUpdate.behavio.commonMistakes: Forgetting memoryUpdate expectations when the bad case is about learned behavior.

eval.expectedOutput.memoryUpdate.pattern.whyNecessary: Pattern notes should preserve useful behavior context without over-storing personal detail.
eval.expectedOutput.memoryUpdate.pattern.productImpact: Improves future AI Check context quality.
eval.expectedOutput.memoryUpdate.pattern.validation: Exact checks exact string or null; phrase checks are case-insensitive.
eval.expectedOutput.memoryUpdate.pattern.commonMistakes: Requiring exact prose when topic coverage is enough.

eval.tags.meaning: Risk and category labels for filtering eval results.
eval.tags.whyNecessary: PM Review and eval reporting need grouped risk views.
eval.tags.productImpact: Drives case sets and tag-level pass rates.
eval.tags.validation: Must be an array; recommended tags are shared in PM Review.
eval.tags.commonMistakes: Using tags to encode expected behavior instead of assertions.

eval.reviewerNote.whyNecessary: Reviewer notes preserve the product reasoning behind a case.
eval.reviewerNote.productImpact: Improves future prompt/schema review and case cleanup.
eval.reviewerNote.commonMistakes: Putting machine-checked expectations only in reviewerNote instead of expectedOutput.

status.meaning: PM Review lifecycle status for the case.
status.whyNecessary: Default eval runs and PM queues need to know whether a case is active, release-gating, or archived.
status.productImpact: Controls which cases appear in active, draft, regression, and archive views.
status.validation: Must be one of the known case statuses.
status.commonMistakes: Using regression for unfinished cases or hard-deleting stale cases instead of archiving.

archivedAt.meaning: Archive timestamp when the case has been retired.
archivedAt.whyNecessary: Archived cases should remain traceable without running by default.
archivedAt.productImpact: Preserves review history while keeping normal eval runs clean.
archivedAt.validation: Present only when status is archived.
archivedAt.commonMistakes: Leaving archivedAt on a regression case.

archivedReason.meaning: Optional explanation for archiving the case.
archivedReason.whyNecessary: PMs need to know why a case was retired.
archivedReason.productImpact: Reduces duplicate case re-creation and preserves decision context.
archivedReason.commonMistakes: Archiving without explaining what replaced or invalidated the case.
